'''Suman Kumar Dhar''' (born 1968) is an Indian molecular biologist and a professor  at the ''Special Centre for Molecular Medicine'' of [[Jawaharlal Nehru University]].<ref name="Winners of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Awards 2012">{{cite web | url=https://ias.org.in/2012/09/winners-of-shanti-swarup-bhatnagar.html | title=Winners of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Awards 2012 | publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences | date=28 September 2012 | access-date=2 November 2016}}</ref> He is known for his studies on the [[DNA replication]] and [[cell cycle regulation]] in [[Helicobacter pylori]] and [[Plasmodium falciparum]], two pathogens affecting humans.<ref name="Brief Profile of the Awardee">{{cite web | url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/content/Detail.aspx?AID=139 | title=Brief Profile of the Awardee | publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize | date=2016 | access-date=5 October 2016}}</ref> An elected fellow of the [[National Academy of Sciences, India]], Indian National Science Academy<ref name="Indian fellow">{{cite web | url=http://insaindia.res.in/detail.php?id=P16-1715 | title=Indian fellow | publisher=Indian National Science Academy | date=2016 | access-date=2 November 2016}}</ref> and the Indian Academy of Sciences,<ref name="Fellow Profile">{{cite web | url=http://www.ias.ac.in/describe/fellow/Dhar,_Prof._Suman_Kumar | title=Fellow Profile | publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences | date=2016 | access-date=2 November 2016}}</ref> he is also a recipient of the [[National Bioscience Award for Career Development]] of the [[Department of Biotechnology]] in 2010.<ref name="Awardees of National Bioscience Awards for Career Development">{{cite web | url=http://dbtindia.nic.in/wp-content/uploads/2014/03/list_of_bioscience_awardees.pdf | title=Awardees of National Bioscience Awards for Career Development | publisher=Department of Biotechnology | date=2016 | access-date=17 October 2016}}</ref> The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]], the apex agency of the Government of India for scientific research, awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]], one of the highest Indian science awards, in 2012, for his contributions to biological sciences.<ref name="View Bhatnagar Awardees">{{cite web | url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/AwardeeList.aspx | title=View Bhatnagar Awardees | publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize | date=2016 | access-date=12 November 2016}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Suman Kumar Dhar, born on 6 March 1968 in the Indian state of [[West Bengal]], graduated in chemistry from [[Burdwan University]] in 1989 and completed his master's degree in biochemistry in 1992 from [[Kalyani University]] before securing a PhD in molecular biology from [[Jawaharlal Nehru University]] (JNU) in 1998.<ref name="Faculty profile">{{cite web | url=http://www.jnu.ac.in/Faculty/sdhar/cv.pdf | title=Faculty profile | publisher=Jawaharlal Nehru University | date=2016 | access-date=2 November 2016}}</ref>

He worked from 1997 to 1998 as a research assistant at the department of microbiology of the [[University of Nebraska Medical Center]]. Next, he did his post-doctoral studies at [[Brigham and Women’s Hospital]] of [[Harvard Medical School]] which he completed in 2001.<ref name="Decoding deadly pathogens - Dr Suman Kumar Dhar">{{cite web | url=http://www.biospectrumindia.com/biospecindia/features/123058/decoding-deadly-pathogens-i-dr-suman-kumar-dhar-i | title=Decoding deadly pathogens - Dr Suman Kumar Dhar | publisher=Biospectrum India | date=12 December 2012 | access-date=2 November 2016}}</ref>

Returning to India the same year, he joined [[Jawaharlal Nehru University]] as an assistant professor at the ''Special Centre for Molecular Medicine'' (SCMM) of the university where he rose in ranks to become an associate professor in 2005 and a professor in 2011, finally reaching the position of the chairperson of SCMM in 2011. In between, he served as a visiting fellow at Harvard Medical School from 2002 to 2003), the [[Harvard School of Public Health]] from 2003 and 2004, and the  [[Bernhard Nocht Institute for Tropical Medicine]] in 2007. He also served as a Humboldt Research Fellow at Bernhard Nocht Institute in 2008. Besides his academic duties at JNU, Dhar is involved in the establishment of ''Centre of Excellence in Parasitology'', a [[Department of Biotechnology]]-funded project.<ref name="Faculty profile" /> He was also a member of the proctorial committee constituted by JNU to inquire about the [[2016 JNU protests]].<ref name="Afzal Guru protests: Police slap charges of sedition, conspiracy">{{cite web | url=http://indianexpress.com/article/cities/delhi/afzal-guru-protests-police-slap-charges-of-sedition-conspiracy/ | title=Afzal Guru protests: Police slap charges of sedition, conspiracy | publisher=Indian Express | date=12 February 2016 | access-date=2 November 2016}}</ref><ref name="Arrest ‘Anti India Elements’ Says Rajnath, So Police Pin ‘Sedition’ on JNUSU Head">{{cite web | url=http://thewire.in/21455/arrest-anti-india-elements-says-rajnath-so-police-pin-sedition-on-jnusu-head/ | title=Arrest 'Anti India Elements' Says Rajnath, So Police Pin 'Sedition' on JNUSU Head | publisher=The Wire | date=13 February 2016 | access-date=2 November 2016}}</ref>

== Career ==
Dhar's research history starts during his graduate studies when he worked on [[Entamoeba histolytica]], the protozoan which causes [[amoebiasis]], focusing on its ribosomal DNA circle.<ref name="Suman Kumar Dhar, Associate Professor and present Chairperson">{{cite web | url=http://www.jnu.ac.in/SCMM/FacultyProfile.asp | title=Suman Kumar Dhar, Associate Professor and present Chairperson | publisher=JNU - SCMM | date=2016 | access-date=2 November 2016}}</ref> Later at Harvard Medical School, his post-doctoral studies were centered on mammalian DNA replication which assisted him to identify the [[ORC6]] (origin recognition complex subunit six) and its role in viral DNA replication. He also identified [[geminin]], a replication inhibitor, as a blocking factor of viral DNA replication, a discovery which earned him a US patent.<ref name="Faculty profile" /> Later, he studied the human pathogens, [[Helicobacter pylori]] and [[Plasmodium falciparum]] and their DNA replication and cell cycle regulation.<ref name="Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners">{{cite web | url=http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf | title=Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners | publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research | date=1999 | access-date=5 October 2016 | pages=34}}</ref> He also worked on anti-malarial drugs and proposed [[Acriflavine]] as an anti-malarial agent, which has also been patented by him.<ref name="US Patent Issued to Suman Kumar Dhar on June 28 for Method of Screening Anti-Plasmodial Activity of Acriflavin and Acriflavin as an Anti-Malarial Agent ">{{cite web | url=https://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P3-4103625881.html | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180911002438/https://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P3-4103625881.html | url-status=usurped | archive-date=11 September 2018 | title=US Patent Issued to Suman Kumar Dhar on June 28 for "Method of Screening Anti-Plasmodial Activity of Acriflavin and Acriflavin as an Anti-Malarial Agent" | date=28 June 2016 | via=[[HighBeam Research]] | url-access=subscription | work=US Fed News Service, Including US State News | access-date=2 November 2016}}</ref> His work has identified PfGyrase for P. falciparum and HpDnaB helicase for H. pylori as targets<ref name="Suman Kumar Dhar on Global Professor Rank">{{cite web | url=https://globalprofessorrank.com/professor/suman-kumar-dhar/jawaharlal-nehru-university-new-delhi | title=Suman Kumar Dhar on Global Professor Rank | publisher=Global Professor Rank | date=2016 | access-date=2 November 2016}}</ref> and these researches are reported to be helpful in drug discovery efforts for [[Gastric ulcer]]s, [[Gastric adenocarcinoma]]s and Malaria.<ref name="Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Award in Biological Sciences - Suman Dhar">{{cite journal | url=https://indiabioscience.org/news/2012/shanti-swarup-bhatnagar-award-in-biological-sciences-suman-dhar | title=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Award in Biological Sciences - Suman Dhar | author=Ajeena Ramanujan | journal=India Bioscience | date=2 October 2012}}</ref>
Dhar has documented his research by way of a number of articles{{Refn|group=note|Please see ''Selected bibliography'' section}} and online repositories such as [[PubMed]]<ref name="Dhar on PubMed">{{cite web | url=https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=Dhar%20SK%5BAuthor%5D&cauthor=true&cauthor_uid=11509178 | title=Dhar on PubMed | publisher=PubMed | date=2016 | access-date=2 November 2016}}</ref> and Pubfacts have listed many of them.<ref name="Dhar on Pubfacts">{{cite web | url=http://www.pubfacts.com/author/Suman+Kumar+Dhar?tr=1 | title=Dhar on Pubfacts | publisher=Pubfacts | date=2016 | access-date=2 November 2016}}</ref> He has contributed chapters to three books which include ''Epigenetics: Development and Disease'' by [[Tapas Kumar Kundu]].<ref name="Kundu2012">{{cite book|author=Tapas Kumar Kundu|title=Epigenetics: Development and Disease|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=O2OBaKOyavwC&pg=PA659|year=2012|publisher=Springer Science & Business Media|isbn=978-94-007-4525-4|pages=659–}}</ref> He is associated with many science journals such as [[Journal of Biological Chemistry]], [[Molecular Microbiology (journal)|Molecular Microbiology]], [[FEBS Journal]] and [[Medical Science Monitor]] as an ad-hoc reviewer and has delivered featured talks including his oration at the Gordon Research Conference on Host-Parasite interaction held in [[Rhode Island]] in 2012.<ref name="Faculty profile" />

== Awards and honors ==
While in the US, Dhar received two grants for his researches, a grant from the [[National Institutes of Health]] for studies on emerging infectious diseases (1997–98) and the [[United States Department of the Army]] grant for research on breast cancer (2000–03).<ref name="Faculty profile" /> He received the Senior International Research Fellowship of the [[Wellcome Trust]] in 2005, the tenancy of the fellowship extending to 2010, and on its expiry, he received the Wellcome Trust-[[Department of Biotechnology|DBT]] Senior Research Fellowship in 2010. In 2006, Dhar received the Swarnajayanthi Fellowship of the Department of Biotechnology (DBT)<ref name="Swarnajayanthi Fellowship">{{cite web | url=http://dst.gov.in/sites/default/files/sjaward06-07.pdf | title=Swarnajayanthi Fellowship | publisher=Department of Biotechnology | date=2006 | access-date=1 November 2016}}</ref> and four years later, DBT honored him again with the 2010 [[National Bioscience Award for Career Development]].<ref name="Awardees of National Bioscience Awards for Career Development" /> He was elected to the [[Guha Research Conference]] in 2007 and the next year brought him the Alexander Von Humboldt Fellowship and the Swarnajayanti Fellowship of the [[Department of Science and Technology (India)|Department of Science and Technology]].<ref name="SwarnaJayanti Fellowship Awards">{{cite web | url=http://dst.gov.in/sites/default/files/sjaward06-07.pdf | title=SwarnaJayanti Fellowship Awards | publisher=Department of Science and Technology | date=2007 | access-date=3 November 2016}}</ref>

A member of the [[American Society for Microbiology]], Dhar was awarded the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]], one of the highest Indian science awards, by the [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]] in 2012.<ref name="View Bhatnagar Awardees" /> The National Academy of Sciences, India elected him as a fellow in 2011<ref name="NASI fellows">{{cite web | url=http://nasi.nic.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=D | title=NASI fellows | publisher=National Academy of Sciences, India | date=2016 | access-date=2 November 2016}}</ref> and he became a fellow of the [[Indian National Science Academy]] and the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] in 2016.<ref name="Indian fellow" /><ref name="Fellow Profile" />
